summary: Built and filed a probe for a cleaner manifestation of the same cause: a feature-enabled restart of a node that holds no snapshot at all, so the log scan is the only mechanism that could rebuild its membership. In local construction feedback on a live three-node cluster, the follower held zero snapshots with a staged commit index of 12 over a log ending at 13 and reported {A,B,C} while running; restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs it reported an empty configuration (zero servers) even though its FSM had replayed to index 13, while the same restart without the feature reported {A,B,C}. The mechanism is the parent question's scan start, max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1, combined with the replay that raises lastApplied to the persisted commit index — here it skips every configuration entry rather than one, so the node loses its membership instead of keeping a stale one. The probe is registered as a child question of the parent with a sourced hypothesis and discriminator, and filed as an experiment with two admissions over the fixture (zero snapshots, running configuration, ten committed commands) and four comparisons: the feature-enabled restart should report the bootstrap membership (expected violated, twice, once by id list and once by configured-server count) and the feature-off control should report it (expected holds, twice). Incomplete: that receipt and its interpretation, plus the source-derived consequences I deliberately did not execute (a node with an empty configuration will not campaign, and its vote handling treats an empty configuration as a bootstrapping cluster).
